purpose: Howard asked for a budget speaker alternative to JBL and a simple explanation of +/-dB frequency response.
scope: Candidate audible-band speakers for bench evaluation. No assembled acoustic performance or animal protocol is established. No product is qualified for the full SONIC frequency range by these listings.

candidates.package: Pair; built-in amplification; analog 3.5 mm audio input and USB power
candidates.price_observation: Manufacturer search retrieval shows 20.99 USD promotional price and 24.99 USD reference price, with 5.50 USD shipping displayed. Described conversationally as about 21-25 USD per pair before delivery/tax.
candidates.retrieval_limit: Full manufacturer product text and specs recovered via search. Direct opening returned 403. Separate cached catalog availability/price conflicts with the product result; current purchasability and checkout total are unconfirmed.
candidates.role: Much cheaper candidate for selected audible bench tones; reduced high-frequency coverage. Any interface-to-3.5 mm adapter and suitable USB power are additional configuration checks.
candidates.limit: Not a substitute for the paper's tones extending to 27-32 kHz. Published nominal band has no retrieved +/-dB flatness tolerance, and no measured level/distortion/timing at the reference position.

candidates.package: Pair; one powered cabinet drives its passive companion; analog TRS/RCA/3.5 mm connections
candidates.observed_availability: In stock displayed on retrieved retailer page; unreserved
candidates.source_location: Manufacturer manual Appendix B, printed page 18
candidates.limit: Manufacturer uses -3 dB and -10 dB endpoint response labels; do not rewrite these as a verified +/-3 dB whole-band flatness guarantee. Price is for the pair, not a single cabinet. This does not reduce the purchase cost versus one 99 USD JBL.

JBL_reference.observed_availability: In stock, limited-time offer displayed; unreserved
JBL_reference.package: One powered speaker; two would be 198 USD before delivery/tax. Our basic comparison uses one.

plus_minus_db_explanation.meaning: Variation in the speaker's output versus a response reference across the specified frequency band under test conditions, using the same electrical input level. Not a measure of pitch error, timing error or random volume variation from trial to trial.
plus_minus_db_explanation.hypothetical_example: If the response reference were 70 dB SPL, +/-3 dB would correspond to 67-73 dB SPL under that illustration's conditions. This is a teaching example, not a selected exposure level or a prediction for the animal position.
plus_minus_db_explanation.comparison_limit: Smaller +/-dB means a flatter response only when comparing similar frequency bands and measurement conditions. JBL +/-3 dB over 49 Hz-20 kHz and MF1 +/-13 dB over 1-65 kHz cover different bands.
plus_minus_db_explanation.calibration: Measure retained tones at fixed reference geometry and adjust per-frequency waveform levels. This can improve level matching within output/distortion limits; factory response figures are not assembled absolute SPL uncertainty.

screened_but_not_selected.reason: Retailer results conflict between expired 99.99 USD promotion ending October 1 and 114.99 USD listing; neither establishes savings versus one 99 USD JBL.
Manufacturer search listing 139.99 USD, not a cheaper upfront alternative to one 99 USD JBL.

actions: Public-source research only; no purchase, vendor contact, hardware connection or experimental measurement. Earlier budgets and PDFs are unchanged.
